subject: 5-Bullet Friday — How to Get Unstuck, Life Advice from Ethan Hawke, Music for This Wild Week, and More

bullets.section: Short TED Talk I’m watching once again
bullets.title: Give yourself permission to be creative
bullets.creator: Ethan Hawke
bullets.note: . This clocks in at roughly nine minutes. And thanks to Laird Z. for the recommendation. From the description: “Reflecting on moments that shaped his life, actor [Ethan Hawke](https://www.instagram.com/ethanhawke/?hl=en) examines how courageous expression promotes healing and connection with one another—and invites you to discover your own unabashed creativity. ‘There is no path till you walk it,’ he says.”

bullets.title: So you wanna de-bog yourself
bullets.creator: Adam Mastroianni
bullets.note: . I only just found Adam, but his writing is some of the most hilarious—and helpful—I’ve seen in a long time. Really worth the read. Big thanks to Crazy B for sending this to me.

bullets.title: Nasty
bullets.creator: Polyphia, feat
bullets.note: ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i7UkKEEGgAQ), [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/track/2yWAPCnRMbpbGqVHAZzqgJ)) by [Polyphia](https://polyphia.com/), feat. [Jason Richardson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Richardson_(musician)). This seemed to me like an appropriate soundtrack for the week, no? Give the track a minute or so to warm up, and if you think it’s all synth, think again. [Here’s an unplugged version](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DSBBEDAGOTc) of a track called “Playing God,” featuring lead guitarist Tim Henson. It’s bananas.

bullets.title: Stutz
bullets.note: This doc pairs well with Adam’s “what I’m reading” post above. _Stutz_ was recommended to me by multiple friends, and it does a beautiful job of sharing both a loving relationship and effective therapeutic tools for changing your life. I was hesitant to watch this at first. I worried that it might dredge up old, painful personal issues that I feel I’ve spent enough time on, but it didn’t open Pandora’s box at all. As my friends correctly reassured me, it’s nothing but upside. Here’s the official description: “In candid conversations with actor [Jonah Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonah_Hill), leading psychiatrist [Phil Stutz](https://www.thetoolsbook.com/about-phil-and-barry) explores his early life experiences and unique, visual model of therapy.” Watch the trailer [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UKCmefQdplI).
